questions.question: Compare the roles of the Purchases book and the Sales book in recording business transactions.
questions.solution_html:
• ComparetherolesofthePurchasesbookandtheSalesbookinrecording business
  • transactions.
  • • Purchases Book: Records credit purchases of goods or inventory intended for resale. It
  • focuses solely on transactions where goods are acquired on credit.
  • • Sales Book: Records credit sales of goods or inventory to customers. It captures transactions
  • where goods are sold on credit.
  • • Purchases Book: Indicates an increase in liabilities (creditors) as goods are purchased on
  • credit.
  • • Sales Book: Indicates an increase in assets (debtors) as goods are sold on credit.
  • The Purchases Book and Sales Book play complementary roles in tracking business
  • activities. While the Purchases Book ensures accurate accounting for goods bought on credit,
  • the Sales Book ensures the same for goods sold on credit. Together, they provide essential
  • data for managing a company’s working capital and financial health.

questions.question: What are the primary differences in data presentation between the vertical and horizontal formats of the balance sheet and income statement? (4 × 5 = 20)
questions.solution_html:
• Whataretheprimarydifferencesindatapresentationbetweenthevertical and horizontal
  • formats of the balance sheet and income statement?
  • Vertical Format:
  • • Data is presented in a top-to-bottom sequence.
  • • Items are listed in a single column, grouped and marshalled logically.
  • • Easier to read and aligns with modern financial reporting standards, such as IFRS and
  • Companies Act, 2013.
  • Horizontal Format:
  • • Data is displayed side-by-side across two columns or sections.
  • • Commonly divides items into debit (left) and credit (right) sides.
  • • Traditional format, less commonly used in modern financial reporting.
